_note: Step-by-step clues for Signs and Symbols (Chapter 18): the book questions and the past-paper questions filed under the chapter, by question id. Each list says where the = (or < or >) probably goes, works out part of each side or rules out a wrong option, and leaves the last check to the student: it never names the right option. Questions marked needs-review have none. tools/check_clues.ts checks them.

ss-b01: The middle sign compares the two sides (=, < or >). Work out each side on its own.
Option B gives 6 + 8 > 9 + 7, that is 14 > 16. False.
Try the other options the same way. Which one is true?
ss-b02: All four numbers are elevens: 22, 33, 66 and 11 are 2, 3, 6 and 1 elevens.
So 22 + 33 and 66 − 11 are equal. Which option gives those signs, in order?
ss-b03: 48 is at both ends. If = goes before the last 48, the left side must come back to 48.
Which option has ÷ and × on the 8s, and then =?
ss-b04: The numbers are small, so the signs are probably + and −. Put = before the 10.
11 − 8 = 3. What must you add to 3 to make 10?
Which option gives those signs, in order?
ss-b05: There are four signs, and one of them is =. Work out each side on its own, × and ÷ first.
3 + 3 = 6. Which option gives those signs, in order?
ss-b06: One sign is =. Work out each side on its own, × and ÷ first.
Which option gives those signs, in order?
ss-b07: One sign compares the two sides (=, < or >). Work out each side on its own, × first.
Option A gives 13 × 5 < 15 ÷ 5 × 9, that is 65 < 27. False.
Try the other options the same way. Which one is true?
ss-b08: 47 is the biggest number and comes last, so = probably goes just before it.
30 + 17 = 47. Which option gives those signs, in order?
ss-b09: One sign compares the two sides. Work out each side on its own, × first.
Option A gives 23 = 8 + 4 × 21 − 7. The right side is 8 + 84 − 7 = 85, so it says 23 equals 85. False.
Try the other options the same way. Which one is true?
ss-b10: One sign is =. Work out each side on its own, × and ÷ first.
35 × 14 ÷ 7 = 35 × 2. Which option gives those signs, in order?
ss-b11: 28 comes twice at the end, so = is probably between them.
14 + 14 = 28. Which option gives those signs, in order?
ss-b12: As printed, the right side 7 + 36 ÷ 54 − 5 is not even a whole number, so something must change.
91 = 7 × 13, so 91 ÷ 7 = 13 would be neat. That needs a ÷ right after 91.
Which swap puts ÷ after 91? Then check: is 91 ÷ 7 + 36 equal to 54 − 5?
ss-b14: As printed, 9 ÷ 27 is a fraction (1/3), so the left side is not a whole number.
28 = 7 + 21, and 21 = 3 × 7. You need a 3 from 9 and 27.
27 ÷ 9 = 3. Which swap gives that? Check the left side after it.
ss-b15: Make the product smaller: 14 × 5 = 70. Then you need 11 more, and 22 ÷ 2 = 11.
Which swap gives 14 × 5 + 22 ÷ 2? Check that it is 81.
